Voice Labels Case

A desk console for the Raspberry Pi label printer. The 7" screen reclines 20° above a sloped deck holding the TALK and PRINT buttons. A closed power pod behind the base holds the USB power brick and a switched, fused mains socket. The housing and pod join the base with sliding dovetails, and the back plate, pod lid and deck are sliding panels: no screws. Click a part to take it apart by hand: pins turn and pull out, panels slide, buttons press, and the housing, screen and pod come off once whatever holds them is out of the way. Tick Spread apart for an exploded view. Drag to turn the model, scroll or pinch to zoom.

How it joins

Housing to baseTwo dovetail rails under the housing slide down the seat into slots in the base
Pod to baseDrops onto two vertical dovetail rails on the back of the base
PanelsBack plate slides down from the top, pod lid slides in from the back, deck slides in from the front (with the front panel lowered, since the buttons hang below it), and the front panel slides up from underneath; each clicks into place
LocksFour quarter-turn lock pins, two per part, through the side walls and across grooves in the rails. Turn a pin's wing head upright to unlock it and pull it out
Power socketA printed keeper frame over its front plate, held by two short quarter-turn pins through the pod's back wall

Openings

Mic openingRight side wall, low: the mic plugs straight into the Pi's USB port behind it
Cable tabsSnap-out notches on both sides, high (power) and middle (printer, right side)
Wire slotHousing floor, button wires up to the Pi
VentsBack plate, over the Pi's fan; pod back wall and lid, over the brick
Power socketPod back wall: IEC C14 with switch and fuse, 47 × 27.4 mm cutout, clamped by the keeper frame
Cable holeØ30 mm, right side: pod front wall through to the space under the buttons
USB-C cableThrough the cable hole and up the housing's wire slot, or from the notch at the top of the pod to the notch at the top of the back plate

How the pins lock

Close-up of one pin and a piece of the wall, shown see-through so you can watch the lug behind it. Drag to turn.
Loading…
  1. Hold the pin with its wing head upright, lined up with the slot at the top of the hole, and push it in. The lug on the shaft passes through the slot.
  2. Turn the head a quarter turn, either way. Behind the wall the lug rides up a small ramp, pulling the head tight against the wall.
  3. At 90° the lug drops into a notch with a click. Locked: it can't pull out, and it can't turn back by itself. A stop just past the notch stops it going too far.
  4. To unlock, twist the head back to upright. It takes a firm twist to get the lug back over the ramp.
  5. Pull the pin out.

The same lock is on all ten pins: two hold the housing on the base, two hold the pod, four hold the screen in the housing, and two hold the power socket's keeper frame. Head crosswise means locked.
